summary: Resume-after-split: fragmented final choice and duplicate leading tokens after rapid reconnect loop (websocket)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Brightscribe Labs) reports that after a flurry of short websocket disconnects from a browser client behind a corporate load balancer, resumed streams sometimes contain: duplicated leading tokens (prefix repeated), and the final choice is split into two fragments where the final fragment is missing the closing punctuation and metadata. This appears most frequently when reconnects occur within 400ms of each other (rapid reconnect loop).

Impact:
- Some user-facing responses appear to have repeated prefixes which confuse downstream parsing in the customer's client.
- Final choice missing trailing punctuation/metadata causes their post-processing (choice-ranking + telemetry tagging) to fail intermittently.
- Customer is on Dedicated tier and reports this impacts a small percentage (~0.6%) of streaming responses during peak traffic.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: us-east, GPU-backed serving nodes (A10G equivalent).
- Client: Chrome 113 in a single-page app with background auto-reconnect enabled by customer code.
- Network path: customer LB -> corporate proxy -> Redwood API Gateway -> streaming runtime.

Steps to reproduce (as reported):
1) Initiate streaming chat request via websocket.
2) Trigger rapid disconnects by toggling offline/online in browser or simulating flaky proxy (disconnects spaced ~200-400ms).
3) Allow client to auto-reconnect and resume stream using lastSeenTokenOffset semantics.
4) Observe response: sometimes prefix duplicated and final choice split/truncated.

Observed behavior:
- Reconnect resume creates an extra initial fragment that contains tokens already sent before the disconnect.
- The final choice is emitted in two separate "choice" frames: the first part appears as normal partial content, the second arrives but lacks trailing meta (no "finish_reason" and missing punctuation).
- No 5xx errors in API gateway logs during incidents; proxy logs show a flurry of CONNECT/TEARDOWN.

Expected behavior:
- Resume should stitch seamlessly without re-sending tokens already acknowledged by client.
- Final choice should be emitted complete with finish_reason and punctuation retained.

Initial hypothesis:
- Race between prefix cache eviction (KV cache) and resume reconciliation logic when reconnects happen faster than our resume window; client ack offsets may drift causing duplicated slices.
- Proxy or LB may be splitting frames or introducing micro-reordering that our websocket resume code does not currently guard against.

Attachments / links:
- Customer-provided minimal repro app (link shared to S3 in private exchange).
- Logs snapshot: s3://redwood-support-uploads/sup-99760/logs-2026-03-09-14z.txt
- Dashboard snapshots: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/sessions/resume-metrics?orgId=1&var-env=prod
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Aisha Kapoor: Created ticket after initial CS call. Customer provided example message IDs and approximate timestamps where duplication occurred. Asked for request/response ids and session ids.

2026-03-10 11:05 - Marco Silva: ACK. Assigned to infra-rt team. Requested customer to reproduce with verbose client logging enabled and to capture websocket frames via browser devtools or tcpdump behind proxy.

2026-03-10 15:32 - Brightscribe Support (Elena Park): We reproduced this 2x in a short test. Uploaded pcap and devtools HAR to our secure bucket. Observed that our client accepted the duplicate tokens as new content (no de-dup on client).

2026-03-11 07:44 - Marco Silva: First-pass triage: no gateway 5xx, no serving-runtime error. Noticed increased resume events for same session id in logs. Added labels and requested a correlating trace id from telemetry team.

2026-03-11 13:22 - SRE (Jon Chu): Found a pattern: websocket keepalive timeouts at the LB were set to 30s but the proxy between LB and gateway had a 1s aggressive idle-reap for half-open sockets, which caused frequent mid-stream TCP resets when load peaked. Opening a ticket with networking to investigate policy for long-lived streams.

2026-03-12 10:09 - Marco Silva: Running a local repro using our internal flaky-proxy tool to reproduce accelerated disconnects. Observed duplicated prefix when reconnect occurs within 250-450ms. Added this reproduction to linked GitHub issue.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11: Collected session-level event trace for affected session ids. Resume offsets in event stream show two resume attempts with overlapping token ranges (offsets 0-128 then 100-230) — indicates stale last-ack value on resume request.

2026-03-11: Verified KV cache TTL is 60s and is not expiring in observed windows. Kernel-level TCP resets from proxy cause the runtime to treat subsequent resume as new session in some code paths leading to fragment duplication.

2026-03-12: Temporarily reproduced with internal flaky-proxy and added extra guard in resume logic to dedupe overlapping token ranges — local test reduced duplication occurrences by ~95% in synthetic runs.

2026-03-12: Hypothesis refinement: two issues compound — aggressive proxy TCP teardown leading to raced resume attempts, and resume reconciliation code that appends fragments when offsets slightly overlap instead of trimming duplicates.
resolution_summary: In progress. Short-term mitigation: advising customer to increase client-side backoff to avoid rapid auto-reconnects and coordinate with their proxy team to relax idle-reap settings. Engineering has a targeted patch (serving-runtime PR #1289) that adds defensive de-duplication for overlapping resume offsets and stricter validation of finish_reason propagation. Patch is in code review and test plan includes end-to-end repro with flaky-proxy. Next steps: land PR, deploy to canary dedicated pool, monitor resume-metrics for reduction in duplicate-prefix and missing-final-choice events. Customer notified and offered temporary guidance and higher-frequency monitoring.
next_steps: Merge PR 1289 and run canary rollout to a subset of dedicated pools (target: us-east small subset)
Coordinate with Networking team to confirm proxy idle-reap behavior and recommend settings to Brightscribe (CP: Jon Chu)
Ask customer to apply client backoff patch to avoid auto-reconnect loops while we validate fix
Monitor grafana panel 'sessions/resume-metrics' for drop in duplicated-prefix rate to <0.1% for Brightscribe pool
